name: ABBV-295

lead: ABBV-295 is an experimental amylin analogue injected under the skin, developed by AbbVie for obesity.
Registered trials include several Phase 1 studies and a Phase 2 trial of about 360 adults. No results are public.

paras: Amylin analogues mimic the hormone amylin, which promotes satiety and slows gastric emptying.
Safety data are not published. The drug is unapproved.

lead: ABBV-295 (also GUB014295) is an investigational amylin analogue given by subcutaneous injection, being developed by AbbVie for obesity. It is not approved.[1][2]

Registered trials include Phase 1 studies in adults with obesity, in Japanese participants with overweight or obesity, and in women taking oral contraceptives, and a Phase 2 trial in 360 adults with obesity or overweight and weight-related comorbidities that began recruiting in August 2026.[3][2][4][5] No results have been published. A registered psoriasis study lists targeted therapies and is not described as an ABBV-295 efficacy trial.[6]

paras: Phase 1 trial NCT07291232 (about 80 adults with obesity) assesses adverse events and pharmacokinetics and began in November 2025.[2] NCT07514260 studies about 24 Japanese participants and NCT07414784, a completed study of about 20 women, examines interaction with oral contraceptives.[3][5] Phase 2 trial NCT07752979 is recruiting about 360 adults.[4] Results have not been published.
A 2026 review of amylin analogues for obesity provides class background.[1]

timeline.event: Phase 1 trial in adults with obesity begins.[2]
Further Phase 1 studies and a Phase 2 obesity trial are registered.[3][4][5]
